Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Livingston
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/03/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 13 as introduced limits the authority of a municipality or county to regulate the installation and use of battery-charged fences, as defined in this bill which could decrease potential receipts to municipal and county general funds by an undetermined amount dependent on the level at which the county or municipality would charge permits or fees for installation or use of a battery-charged fence.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development

Committee: County and Municipal Government
Sponsor: Livingston
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 13 as passed the Senate limits the authority of a municipality or county to regulate the installation and use of battery-charged fences, as defined in this bill which could decrease potential receipts to municipal and county general funds by an undetermined amount dependent on the level at which the county or municipality would charge permits or fees for installation or use of a battery-charged fence.
Reed Ingram, Chair
County and Municipal Government

Committee: County and Municipal Government
Sponsor: Melson
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 02/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 56 as passed the Senate allows counties and municipalities that provide solid waste services to use funds in its solid waste reserve account over $1 million for any lawful purpose in the best interest of the locality.
This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Reed Ingram, Chair
County and Municipal Government
